quote: Suppose that Vj has the MoD with parameter δj for j = 1, 2. Let Hj(v; δj) be the CDF and hj(v; δj) be the PDF of Vj. Then V1 is said to be stochastically smaller than V2 with respect to likelihood ratio order (say V1 ≤lr V2), if h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2) is a decreasing function ∀ v values. ... Then, for δ2 < δ1, we obtain d/dv log [h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2)] < 0 ∀v ≥ 0. So, d/dv log[h1(v;δ1)/h2(v;δ2)] is decreasing in v and consequently V1 ≤lr V2.
family: Monsef distribution MoD(δ): pdf h(v;δ) ∝ δ³(v+1)² e^{−δv}/[δ(δ+2)+2]
ambiguity: Unnumbered display-block claim in the 'Stochastic Ordering' subsection; log-ratio derivative stated as decreasing (the derivative of log-ratio being negative is what makes the ratio decreasing — wording slightly garbled in print).
